question.problem: Find the radius of curvature for the curve $r(t)=(1+{t}^{2})^{2}\,i+t\,j$ at $t=0.$
question.worked_solution:
The curvature $κ(t)$ of a plane curve $r(t)=x(t)\,i+y(t)\,j$ is given by

$$
κ(t)=\frac{|{x}^{′}(t){y}^{″}(t)-{y}^{′}(t){x}^{″}(t)|}{([{x}^{′}(t)]^{2}+[{y}^{′}(t)]^{2})^{3/2}}.
$$

The radius of curvature $R$ is defined as
$R(t)=\frac{1}{κ(t)}.$

Along our curve, we have

$$
x(t)=(1+{t}^{2})^{2},\,y(t)=t.
$$

First, we calculate the derivatives of the components:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{′}(t) & =4t(1+{t}^{2}),\, & {y}^{′}(t) & =1 \\ {x}^{″}(t) & =12{t}^{2}+4,\, & {y}^{″}(t) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting these into the formula for the curvature, we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}κ(t) & =\frac{|4t(1+{t}^{2})\cdot 0-1\cdot (12{t}^{2}+4)|}{{((4t(1+{t}^{2}))^{2}+{1}^{2})}^{3/2}} \\  & =\frac{12{t}^{2}+4}{{((4t(1+{t}^{2}))^{2}+1)}^{3/2}}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the curvature at $t=0$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}κ(0) & =\frac{12(0)^{2}+4}{{((4(0)(1+(0)^{2}))^{2}+1)}^{3/2}} \\  & =\frac{4}{{(0+1)}^{3/2}} \\  & =4.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the radius of curvature at $t=0$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}R(0) & =\frac{1}{κ(0)}=\frac{1}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$
